sentences.text: As a member of the troodontid family, Linhevenator possessed sickle-claws, raptorial hands, and high encephalization quotients indicating advanced behavior and keen senses.
It possessed a second toe similar to dromaeosaurids that carried a sickle-claw larger than those found in basal troodontids.
The first toe of Linhevenator was preserved in a lateral position rather than pointing forward.
The species Linhevenator tani was named and described in 2011 by Xu Xing, Tan Qingwei, Corwin Sullivan, Han Fenglu, and Xiao Dong.
The generic name Linhevenator combines a reference to the Linhe region with the Latin word for hunter, while the species name honors Professor Tan Lin.
Linhevenator was classified as a derived troodontid in a phylogenetic analysis, appearing in a polytomy with Troodon and a clade containing Zanabazar and Saurornithoides.

Researchers view Linhevenator's position as evidence of an evolutionary trend in Troodontidae involving the shortening of forelimbs and parallel evolution of large foot claws in both troodontids and dromaeosaurids.
Linhevenator lived during the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) in the Bayan Mandahu Formation of Bayan Mandahu, Inner Mongolia, China.
The time range for Linhevenator is estimated to be between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
